title: Batch Cartographer: continuous workload fingerprinting, heuristic recommendations and guarded rollout
creator: Sophie Chen
description: Create a lightweight continuous profiling and recommendation service (Batch Cartographer) that maps per-customer and per-route workload signatures and produces ranked batching + KV-cache recommendations. The service must include proactive drift detection, an offline impact simulator (cost/latency/quality), and a guarded rollout mechanism (shadow apply + canary + automatic rollback heuristics).
motivation: Current manual tuning for batching and KV caching is slow and error-prone. Many customers could reduce token cost by 10-40% with safer, automated recommendations. We need a system that generates high-confidence suggestions and applies them incrementally with measurable safety checks.
design_notes: Fingerprint model: combine request payload size distributions, sequence length histograms, KV cache hit patterns, arrival inter-arrival times, and client-level priority tags into a compact signature (<=128 bytes).

Heuristics engine: rule-based priors + lightweight ML ranker for recommendation scoring. Prioritize conservative batch size increases, cache TTL, and prefix caching thresholds where SLOs are preserved.
Simulation: offline replay of sampled trace against candidate config using our runtime cost model (kernel latency curves + batching model) to estimate cost delta and 99th/95th latency tails.

Safe apply flow: 1) generate recommendation with confidence score; 2) shadow-apply (no traffic impact) to validate metrics; 3) small canary rollout (1-5%); 4) monitor for regressions for N minutes; 5) automatic rollback on configured triggers.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Build fingerprint collector and storage (64-bit hash + small histogram blobs). Integrate with agent telemetry to emit per-route signatures every 10 minutes.
Phase 2: Heuristics and scoring service. Implement conservative rule set (safety-first) and a candidate generator for batch size / cache TTL / prefix thresholds.
Phase 3: Offline replay simulator using recent trace samples and runtime latency model. Produce cost/latency delta estimates and a risk score.
Phase 4: Guarded rollout controller: shadow apply, canary percentage API, regression detectors, and rollback automation. Wire into Console with explainability UI.
Phase 5: Pilot with 3 internal tenants and one external beta customer; iterate heuristics and thresholds based on telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Service produces recommendations for at least 90% of profiled routes during pilot window.
Simulated cost delta validated against shadow-apply within +/-10% for 80% of cases.
Guarded rollout executes shadow apply and canary for every automated change; automatic rollback triggers on defined SLI regressions (latency P95 increase >15% or error rate >0.5%).
Console shows per-recommendation explainability (why change, estimated savings, risk score) and a single-click schedule/apply option for manual review.
No customer-facing incidents caused by automated applies during pilot (rollback executed within threshold if triggered).
testing_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint normalization and equivalence (lossless within tolerance).
E2E shadow-apply runs using real traces from prod-replay cluster. Compare simulated vs observed cost/latency deltas.
Chaos tests: intentionally increase load and inject latency to validate rollback heuristics and canary gating logic.
Load test the heuristics service to sustain recommendation generation for 10k routes/hour with <200ms latency.

open_questions: Q1: What is the acceptable time window for canary monitoring (15m vs 60m) for different customer tiers?
Q2: Should recommendations include model-quantization-aware adjustments (different kernels may change batching efficiency)?
Q3: How to encode privacy constraints for VPC/private deployments so fingerprints do not leave customer boundary?
Q4: What guardrail threshold for quality degradation (n-gram overlap / semantic eval) do we require for chat-generation routes?
rollback_plan: 1) On regression detection during canary: immediate revert to previous config and escalate to SRE-runbook.
2) Post-rollback: capture trace, annotated metrics, and store as a counterexample in fingerprint store to prevent re-suggestion.
3) Automatic ticket creation for manual triage if rollback triggered more than 2x in 7 days for same route.
4) Optional manual rollback button in Console for human operators with reason logging.
risk: Medium — risk of transient P95 regressions during canary phases mitigated by conservative thresholds and short canary windows. Privacy risk for private tenants handled by local-only fingerprint aggregation.
